subject: Post-call recap: Nexora pilot scope, evaluation charter, and metric ledger
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@nexora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Nexora pilot scope, evaluation charter, and metric ledger

Thanks again for the call this morning, Sara — good alignment across scope and success needs. I wanted to capture the evaluation charter we discussed so we have a single source of truth before the kickoff. I attached a lightweight metric ledger (metric-ledger-template.xlsx) and a sample workload JSON that we can use to provision the sandbox.

High-level plan (2-week sandbox + 2-week validation):
- Week 0 (this week): Redwood provisions a dedicated sandbox (private model variant, isolated namespace), we ingest 1K sample requests from Nexora.
- Week 1: Run load/latency sweep and functional quality sampling.
- Week 2: Validate cost/token under representative workload and run edge-case prompt set.
- Week 3-4: Longer validation with customer integration tests and acceptance handoff.

Proposed success metrics (must-haves to move to pilot):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 250 ms for single-turn text gen (with 2k context), target 200 ms.
- Throughput: Sustained 120 requests/sec with tail-latency guardrails (P99 <= 800 ms) during representative workload.
- Cost: End-to-end cost <= $0.40 per 1k tokens for the validated model variant (including tokenization, batching, and infra amortization).
- Quality: Domain prompt evaluation: mean score >= 0.80 across 200 sampled prompts (human-reviewed rubric); hallucination rate < 2% on the same sample.

Gating and roll-forward policy:
- Soft gate: quality >= 0.75 AND cost < $0.50 per 1k tokens -> allow extended validation.
- Hard gate: quality >= 0.80 AND latency/throughput targets met -> recommend pilot rollout and capacity commit.
- Rollback: if hallucination rate > 5% or P95 latency > 500 ms in steady-state, we pause rollout and investigate.

Owners (initial):
- Redwood technical lead: Ben Carter — infra/ops and load testing.
- Redwood ML lead: Karthik Iyer — model/quantization profile and quality tuning.
- Nexora PM: Sara Li — acceptance criteria and integration tests.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Sara: share 1,000 representative request logs and the integration test spec by Tues EOD (Jun 8).
2) Redwood (Ben): provision sandbox + initial model variant and share access (expected by Wed Jun 9).
3) Redwood (Karthik): baseline evaluation run and populate metric ledger with initial numbers (deliverable: Jun 11).

Please review the metric ledger and the sample workload attached. If this looks right I will schedule the kickoff for Wed Jun 9 at 10am PT and include a 30-minute ops/validation checkpoint.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear write-up and the artifacts. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- We can provide the 1,000 request logs by EOD Tue (Jun 8). They will include raw request/response pairs and token counts.
- For cost accounting, can you confirm whether the $0.40 / 1k tokens target should include both prompt + completion tokens and any infra overhead (eg, hot-cache overhead)? Our finance team wants an apples-to-apples comparison for our internal cost models.

Also, we have a compliance check that needs to run before full data access — I CC'ed platform@nexora.ai; they will start the service account onboarding once we confirm the sandbox plan.

On the metrics themselves, the latency and throughput targets look reasonable as a starting point. For quality scoring, we'll share our rubric — we typically use a 3-person blind review average and can mirror your rubric for comparability.

Thanks — Sara

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Nexora pilot scope, evaluation charter, and metric ledger

Looping in some operational detail and a suggested timeline I will own. Ben here — happy to run the provisioning and the load sweep. Notes: 
- Sandbox plan: 2x A100-equivalent instances with autoscale buffer for the first two load tests, isolated VPC peering and token redaction in the CLI.
- Workload: we'll take the 1,000 sample logs and run a representative mixture: 60% short requests (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512). We'll record per-request tokens and model-side CPU/GPU utilization.

Acceptance gating (detailed):
- Latency: P95 <= 250 ms for the short+medium mix. If medium+long exceed P95 350 ms, mark for optimization.
- Throughput: sustained 120 rps for a 10-minute window with less than 5% request failures. P99 guardrail <= 800 ms.
- Cost: we will compute cost = infra (GPU hours amortized) + token cost. We'll provide a line-item ledger so Nexora can map to their cost model. If the combined cost > $0.50 / 1k tokens we will list optimization options (quantization, batching, routing to cheaper variant).
- Quality: we'll run automated pass/fail tests (syntactic checks, hallucination detectors) and then a 200-sample human review. Pass threshold: mean >= 0.80.

Timeline (owned by Redwood):
- Jun 8 (Tue): Nexora delivers logs.
- Jun 9 (Wed): Redwood provisions sandbox; kickoff call 10:00am PT.
- Jun 10-11 (Thu-Fri): baseline evaluation runs and metric ledger population.
- Jun 14-18 (Mon-Fri): extended validation and I/O integration tests.
- Jun 21 (Mon): readout and acceptance decision.

I will attach a short runbook to the Drive folder for how we compute the cost lines. Also please confirm whether Nexora wants us to include soft-fallback to a smaller model for cost comparisons (that will change the quality numbers).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
